mainTopic: Mats as סכך and as כלים; the new פרק on sleeping under a bed in the סוכה and what counts as an אהל
overview: This amud finishes the discussion of mats (חוצלות). Everyone agrees that mats of אושא can become טמא and mats of טבריא cannot, and the dispute is only about ordinary mats from other places. The גמרא settles an apparent contradiction in רבי דוסא's view: a mat with a raised edge (גדנפא) is a כלי, and a flat mat is not. A ברייתא about mats of papyrus, bulrushes, sackcloth and horsehair leads the גמרא to find a non-sitting use for each material, in two versions, under each definition of חוצלות. Then the practical law: a flat mat (בודיא) may be used as סכך, but a mat with a raised edge or wall may not, as רב חסדא, עולא and a ברייתא confirm. The first פרק ends with a הדרן. The new פרק opens with a משנה: one who sleeps under a bed in the סוכה has not fulfilled his obligation. רבי יהודה disagrees, and רבי שמעון answers him with the story of טבי. The גמרא limits the משנה to a bed ten טפחים high, then brings a dispute about whether a natural covering counts as an אהל, and asks for רבי יהודה's source, which comes on the next amud.

steps.title: The agreed cases: mats of אושא and mats of טבריא
steps.stepSummary: Both sides agree that mats of אושא are טמאות and mats of טבריא are טהורות.
steps.simpleTranslation: …that they are impure, and the mats of טבריא, that they are pure.
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining the end of a teaching that lists the cases where both sides agree. Mats made in אושא can become טמא, and mats made in טבריא cannot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Mats from אושא were made for people to sit or lie on, so they count as כלים and can become טמא. Mats from טבריא were made only for walls and roofing, so they are not כלים and stay טהור. These two clear cases become the comparison points for the dispute that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: able to become ritually impure, or impure
ritually pure; not able to become impure
טבריא, a town whose coarse mats were made for walls and roofing
אושא, a town whose mats were made for sitting and lying

steps.confusionAlert: This amud starts in the middle of a sentence. The words 'that they are impure' are about the mats of אושא, which were mentioned on the previous amud.

phrases.english: that they are impure (the mats of Usha),
phrases.notes: Continues a sentence that began on the previous amud.

phrases.english: and those of Tiberias, that they are pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a teaching that started earlier.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Mats of אושא can become טמא; mats of טבריא are טהור.

steps.title: Where exactly is the dispute?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which mats the two sides disagree about. The answer: mats from all other places.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what did they disagree? About the rest of the places.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which mats the dispute is really about, and answers right away: mats made anywhere other than אושא or טבריא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the clear cases are set aside, only the in-between case is left. These are ordinary mats that are not clearly made for sitting and not clearly made for roofing.

phrases.english: About what did they disagree?
About the rest of the places.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the dispute after the agreed cases were set out.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which mats are the subject of the dispute?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Mats from every place other than אושא and טבריא.

steps.title: The reasoning of each side
steps.stepSummary: One side compares ordinary mats to those of טבריא (pure). The other side compares them to those of אושא (impure).
steps.simpleTranslation: One Sage holds: since no one sits on them, they are like the mats of טבריא. And the other Sage holds: since it happens that people sit on them, they are like the mats of אושא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the logic of each side. The question is which of the two clear cases ordinary mats are more like.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים say that people do not usually sit on these mats, so they are like the mats of טבריא and stay טהור. רבי דוסא says that people do sometimes sit on them, so they are like the mats of אושא and can become טמא. The dispute comes down to whether occasional sitting is enough to make a mat a כלי.
steps.whatToRemember: The dispute is about ordinary mats. The חכמים look at regular use (no sitting, so טהור). רבי דוסא looks at occasional use (sometimes sitting, so טמא).

phrases.aramaic: מָר סָבַר: כֵּיוָן דְּלֵיכָּא דְּיָתֵיב עֲלַיְיהוּ —
phrases.english: One Sage holds: since there is no one who sits on them —
phrases.notes: This is the view of the חכמים.

phrases.english: they are comparable to those of Tiberias (pure),

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר סָבַר: כֵּיוָן דְּמִקְּרֵי וְיָתְבִי עֲלַיְיהוּ —
phrases.english: and the other Sage holds: since it happens that people sit on them —
phrases.notes: This is the view of רבי דוסא.

phrases.english: they are comparable to those of Usha (impure).

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר סָבַר: כֵּיוָן דְּלֵיכָּא דְּיָתֵיב עֲלַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the dispute identified in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Ordinary mats: the חכמים say they are טהור because no one regularly sits on them. רבי דוסא says they are טמא because people sometimes sit on them.

steps.title: Quoting רבי דוסא's ruling from the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: רבי דוסא says all mats can become טמא through טומאת מת.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: All mats can become impure with corpse impurity; these are the words of רבי דוסא.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא quotes רבי דוסא's ruling from the משנה so it can question it in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If every mat can become טמא, then every mat is a כלי. That would mean no mat may be used as סכך, and this sets up a clash with another source.

keyTerms.meaning: the Master said; a formula for quoting an earlier source
impurity that comes from a corpse

phrases.english: The Master said:
All mats can become impure with corpse impurity,
these are the words of Rabbi Dosa.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: כׇּל הַחוֹצָלוֹת מְטַמְּאִין טְמֵא מֵת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new analysis of the משנה, moving away from the dispute about the mats of אושא and טבריא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי דוסא, all mats can become טמא through טומאת מת.

steps.title: Contradiction: a ברייתא says רבי דוסא agreed that mats are pure
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says רבי דוסא agreed with the view that mats are טהור. This contradicts the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But was it not taught: And likewise רבי דוסא would say in accordance with his words!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the quote from the previous step. A ברייתא says רבי דוסא agreed with רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי that mats are טהור and may be used as סכך.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי דוסא says all mats are טמא. In the ברייתא, he agrees that mats are טהור. Both cannot be true unless the two sources are talking about different kinds of mats.

keyTerms.meaning: but was it not taught (in a ברייתא)?

phrases.english: But was it not taught:

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן הָיָה רַבִּי דּוֹסָא אוֹמֵר כִּדְבָרָיו!
phrases.english: And likewise Rabbi Dosa would say in accordance with his words!
phrases.notes: 'His words' refers to the view of רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי in his father's name, that mats are טהור.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא: וְכֵן הָיָה רַבִּי דּוֹסָא אוֹמֵר כִּדְבָרָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ruling quoted in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי דוסא's ruling that all mats can become טמא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another source has רבי דוסא saying mats are טהור, so his two statements contradict each other.

steps.title: Answer: a mat with a raised edge versus one without
steps.stepSummary: The משנה refers to a mat with a raised edge (גדנפא), which makes it a כלי. The ברייתא refers to a mat without one.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult: this one has a raised edge, and that one does not have a raised edge.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction by explaining that the two sources are talking about two different kinds of mats.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A mat with a raised edge can hold things, so it counts as a כלי and can become טמא. That is the משנה's case. A flat mat without a raised edge is not a כלי, so it stays טהור. That is the ברייתא's case. So רבי דוסא is consistent.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי דוסא, a mat with a raised edge (גדנפא) is a כלי and can become טמא. A flat mat is טהור.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this one (the Mishnah) is a mat that has a raised edge,
that one (the Baraita) is a mat that has no raised edge.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא דְּאִית לֵיהּ גְּדָנְפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: each source refers to a different kind of mat.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two statements of רבי דוסא seemed to be about the same mats and to contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: A mat with a גדנפא can become טמא. A mat without one is טהור.

steps.title: New objection: a ברייתא about mats of different materials
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא. רבי דוסא says mats of these materials get טומאת מת, and the חכמים say they get even טומאת מדרס.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: Mats of papyrus, bulrushes, sackcloth, or horsehair can become impure with corpse impurity; these are the words of רבי דוסא. And the חכמים say: even with treading impurity (מדרס).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new challenge (מיתיבי) by quoting a ברייתא. The exact problem it raises is spelled out next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here רבי דוסא says these mats can become טמא through טומאת מת but not through מדרס, which is the impurity that comes from treading or sitting. The חכמים are stricter and say they can even become טמא through מדרס. If they get טומאת מת but not מדרס, they must be כלים with some use other than sitting. The next step asks whether each explanation of חוצלות can supply such a use.

keyTerms.meaning: they raised an objection (from a ברייתא)
impurity passed on by a זב or similar person treading, sitting, or lying on an object
papyrus or a similar soft plant

steps.confusionAlert: Notice that here the חכמים are stricter than רבי דוסא (they add מדרס). Earlier, the חכמים were the lenient side. Do not assume the same side is always lenient.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
Mats of papyrus and of bulrushes
and of sackcloth and of horsehair —
can become impure with corpse impurity,
these are the words of Rabbi Dosa.
And the Sages say: even with treading impurity.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי: חוֹצָלוֹת שֶׁל שַׁעַם וְשֶׁל גֶּמִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new source whose ruling (טומאת מת without מדרס) is used to test the definitions of חוצלות.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanations of what חוצלות are (מרזובלי vs. מחצלות ממש), and in the first version the view that they are actual mats
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to רבי דוסא, these items get טומאת מת but not מדרס, so they must have a use other than sitting or lying. The next step asks whether each definition of חוצלות can supply such a use for every material.

steps.title: For what use are papyrus and bulrush mats fit, if חוצלות are real mats?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא grants that the מרזובלי explanation can find a use for every material. It then asks what use papyrus and bulrush items would have if חוצלות are flat mats.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well for the one who says they are sacks (מרזובלי). Items of papyrus and bulrushes can be fruit baskets, and items of sackcloth and horsehair can be small sacks and baskets. But for the one who says they are actual mats: sackcloth and horsehair mats can be used as screens and sifters, but what are papyrus and bulrush mats good for?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the view that חוצלות are flat mats. It asks what use papyrus and bulrush mats have that would make them a כלי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי דוסא, these items get טומאת מת but not מדרס. That means they must have some use other than sitting or lying. Under the 'sacks' view, every material has a container use. Under the 'flat mats' view, only sackcloth and horsehair have an obvious use (screens and sifters), so papyrus and bulrushes seem to have none.

keyTerms.meaning: It works well / granted (according to one view)
Sacks or bags (one explanation of חוצלות)
For what are they fit / useful?

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not whether these mats can be used at all. It is whether they have a use other than lying on them. That kind of use is what makes them a כלי for טומאת מת.

phrases.english: Granted, according to the one who says they are sacks (marzovelei),
those of papyrus and of bulrushes
are fit to be a fruit basket;
those of sackcloth and of horsehair
are fit to be small sacks and baskets.
phrases.notes: Their finer weave can hold small items.

phrases.english: But according to the one who says they are actual mats,
granted, those of sackcloth and of horsehair
are fit to be screens and sifters,
but those of papyrus and of bulrushes —
for what are they fit?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ברייתא of step 7 (טומאת מת according to רבי דוסא) to test each definition of חוצלות.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that חוצלות are flat mats (מחצלות ממש)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Getting טומאת מת without מדרס requires a use other than lying. Flat papyrus and bulrush mats seem to have no such use.

steps.title: They are fit as covers for ale vats
steps.stepSummary: Papyrus and bulrush mats can be used to cover vats of ale.
steps.simpleTranslation: They are fit to be used as covers for vats of ale.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by finding a real, non-sitting use for papyrus and bulrush mats.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Covering vats is a use other than lying on the mat. That use makes the mat a כלי, so it can get טומאת מת. With this answer, the 'actual mats' view survives.

keyTerms.meaning: Vats of ale (beer); here, used as covers for them

phrases.english: They are fit as covers for ale vats.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifying a practical use that qualifies the item as a כלי
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Flat papyrus and bulrush mats have no use other than lying, so they could not get טומאת מת.
steps.terutzMaskana: They are used as vat covers, so they are a כלי and get טומאת מת.

steps.title: Second version: the question is asked on the sacks view instead
steps.stepSummary: In another version, the 'actual mats' view is easy, and the question is asked on the מרזובלי view: what use do papyrus and bulrush sacks have?
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: It works well for the one who says actual mats. Papyrus and bulrush mats are vat covers, and sackcloth and horsehair mats are screens and sifters. But for the one who says sacks (מרזובלי): sackcloth and horsehair are small sacks and baskets, but what are papyrus and bulrush items good for?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version (איכא דאמרי) of the same exchange. This time the challenge is aimed at the 'sacks' view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each material and its use stays the same as before. The only change is which view is treated as easy and which one is challenged. In this version, the fruit-basket use is not taken for granted at first.

keyTerms.meaning: Some say (another version of the discussion)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new argument. It is the same question and answer with the two sides switched, so do not look for a new halachic point here.

phrases.english: Some say:
Granted, according to the one who says actual mats,
those of papyrus and of bulrushes
are fit as covers for ale vats;
those of sackcloth and of horsehair
are fit as screens and sifters.
But according to the one who says sacks (marzovelei),
granted, those of sackcloth and of horsehair
are fit as small sacks and baskets,
but those of papyrus and of bulrushes —
for what are they fit?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר מַחְצָלוֹת מַמָּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Restates the step 8 question with the challenged view reversed.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that חוצלות are sacks (מרזובלי)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Papyrus and bulrush sacks seem to have no use that would make them a כלי for טומאת מת.

steps.title: They are fit as fruit baskets
steps.stepSummary: Papyrus and bulrush sacks can be used as fruit baskets.
steps.simpleTranslation: They are fit to be used as a fruit basket.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the second version by naming a container use for papyrus and bulrush items.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A fruit basket is a container, which clearly makes the item a כלי. So the 'sacks' view also survives. In both versions, each side can explain why all four materials get טומאת מת.
steps.whatToRemember: Both explanations of חוצלות hold up. Whether they are flat mats or sacks, every material has some non-sitting use, so they can get טומאת מת according to רבי דוסא.

phrases.english: They are fit as a fruit basket.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifying a practical use that qualifies the item as a כלי
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Papyrus and bulrush sacks have no real use.
steps.terutzMaskana: They serve as fruit baskets, so they are a כלי.

steps.title: רבי חנניה reports that one may roof a סוכה with a mat
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records that an elder in בבל allowed using a mat (בודיא) as סכך, and רבי יהושע agreed.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי חנניה said, 'When I went down to the exile, I found an elder who told me: one may roof a סוכה with a mat. When I came to my uncle רבי יהושע, he agreed with his words.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the practical law of סכך. It brings a ברייתא saying that a mat may be used to roof a סוכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: סכך must not be something that can become טמא. Allowing a mat therefore means this mat is not treated as a כלי. The approval of רבי יהושע gives the ruling of the elder from בבל full authority.

keyTerms.meaning: A woven mat (made of reeds or similar)

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Chananya said:
When I went down to the exile (Babylonia),
I found a certain elder, and he said to me:
One may roof a sukkah with a mat.

phrases.aramaic: וּכְשֶׁבָּאתִי אֵצֶל רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אֲחִי אַבָּא,
phrases.english: And when I came to Rabbi Yehoshua, my father's brother,
he agreed with his words.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the טומאה status of mats to their use as סכך.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may use a mat (בודיא) as סכך.

steps.title: רב חסדא limits this to a mat without a raised edge
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says the mat is allowed only if it has no raised edge.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: This applies only to a mat that has no raised edge.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא adds a limit to the ruling of רבי חנניה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A raised edge makes the mat work like a container, so it becomes a כלי that can become טמא. A flat mat with no edge is not a כלי, so it is valid סכך. This uses the same distinction the גמרא made earlier in step 6.

keyTerms.meaning: And this applies only when (introduces a limiting condition)

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
This applies only where it has no raised edge.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: וְהוּא דְּלֵית לֵיהּ גְּדָנְפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the ruling of step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A mat may be used as סכך only if it has no raised edge (גדנפא).

steps.title: עולא on the mats of מחוזא
steps.stepSummary: עולא says the mats of מחוזא would be valid סכך if not for their raised wall.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: These mats of the people of מחוזא, if not for their wall, one could roof a סוכה with them.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא applies the same rule to a real local case: the mats used in the city of מחוזא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mats of מחוזא are made with a raised wall (קיר). That wall makes them a כלי, so they are not valid as סכך. Without the wall, they would be allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: The people of מחוזא (a city in בבל)
Wall; here, the raised edge of the mat

phrases.english: Ulla said:
These mats of the people of Mechoza,
if not for their wall (raised edge),
one could roof a sukkah with them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר עוּלָּא: הָנֵי בּוּדְיָתָא דִּבְנֵי מָחוֹזָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the limit of רב חסדא to a specific local mat.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The mats of מחוזא are not valid סכך because of their raised wall.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports עולא
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says a mat is valid סכך, but if it has a wall it is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way: One may roof with a mat, but if they have a wall, one may not roof with them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says exactly what עולא said, confirming his ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא states both halves of the rule. A plain mat is allowed, and a mat with a wall is forbidden. This confirms that the raised edge is what decides the law.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way (a supporting ברייתא)

steps.whatToRemember: A flat mat is not a כלי and may be used as סכך. A mat with a raised edge or wall is a כלי, can become טמא, and is not valid as סכך.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical rule for using mats as סכך: whether a mat is valid depends on whether it has a raised edge.

phrases.english: It was also taught this way:
One may roof a sukkah with a mat,
but if they have a wall,
one may not roof with them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the statement of עולא in step 14.
steps.raayaObject: The ruling of עולא that a mat with a wall is not valid סכך
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: מסככין בבודיא, ואם יש להן קיר אין מסככין בהן

steps.title: הדרן — Closing the chapter סוכה
steps.stepSummary: The traditional closing formula marks the end of the first פרק, called סוכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, chapter 'סוכה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The first פרק of the מסכתא ends here with the traditional farewell line. It is not an argument. It is a closing marker.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן is a formula of love and commitment to come back and learn the פרק again. It tells the learner that the discussion of סכך and mats is finished and a new topic is about to begin.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you (closing formula for a chapter)

phrases.english: We will return to you, chapter 'Sukkah'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter that ended with the ברייתא about mats used as סכך.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The first פרק is complete; a new פרק begins.

steps.title: Sleeping under a bed in the סוכה does not fulfill the obligation
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה rules that someone sleeping under a bed inside the סוכה has not fulfilled his obligation.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who sleeps under the bed in the סוכה has not fulfilled his obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: A new פרק opens with a משנה. It says that if you sleep under a bed inside the סוכה, it does not count as sleeping in the סוכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The bed acts like a small tent (אהל) that separates the person from the סכך. So even though he is physically inside the סוכה, he is really sleeping under the bed and not under the סכך.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the whole פרק's theme: anything that blocks a person from the סכך can cancel the מצוה.

phrases.english: One who sleeps under the bed in the sukkah
phrases.notes: These opening words give the new chapter its name.

phrases.english: has not fulfilled his obligation.
phrases.notes: Because the bed is a barrier between him and the סכך.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a brand-new topic in the new פרק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sleeping under a bed in the סוכה does not fulfill the מצוה.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: we used to sleep under beds and the elders said nothing
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה disagrees. He cites a practice of sleeping under beds in front of the זקנים, and they never objected.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said: It was our custom to sleep under the bed in front of the elders, and they did not say anything to us.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה argues against the first opinion. He brings evidence from real life: they slept under beds and the great זקנים never told them they were doing anything wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His proof comes from silence. If the זקנים saw it and said nothing, it must be allowed. That would mean a bed does not count as a barrier that blocks the סכך.

keyTerms.meaning: And they did not say anything to us

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said:
It was our custom that we would sleep
under the bed in front of the elders,
and they did not say anything to us.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents a dissenting opinion, backed by evidence from practice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, sleeping under a bed in the סוכה is acceptable.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: the story of טבי, רבן גמליאל's slave
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון tells of טבי, who slept under the bed. רבן גמליאל explained that טבי did this because, as a slave, he is exempt from סוכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון said: There was an incident with טבי, the slave of רבן גמליאל, who was sleeping under the bed. רבן גמליאל said to the elders: 'Do you see my slave טבי? He is a תלמיד חכם and knows that slaves are exempt from סוכה, so he sleeps under the bed.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון answers רבי יהודה with a story. רבן גמליאל pointed out that his learned slave slept under the bed because he knew he was exempt from the מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point of the story is the reason רבן גמליאל gave. He said טבי slept under the bed *because* he was exempt. That implies a person who is obligated could not sleep under a bed. This is set up as a counter-proof to רבי יהודה's 'they said nothing.'

keyTerms.meaning: An incident or story (used as evidence)
Slaves are exempt from the מצוה of סוכה

steps.confusionAlert: רבן גמליאל was not giving a formal ruling. He was casually praising his slave. The halachic lesson is learned indirectly from his explanation, and the next line spells this out.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon said,

phrases.aramaic: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּטָבִי עַבְדּוֹ שֶׁל רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
phrases.english: There was an incident with Tavi, the slave of Rabban Gamliel,
who was sleeping under the bed,
and Rabban Gamliel said to the elders:
Do you see my slave Tavi,
who is a Torah scholar
and knows that slaves are exempt from the sukkah,
phrases.notes: סוכה is a time-bound positive מצוה, and slaves are exempt from those, like women.

phrases.english: therefore he sleeps under the bed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Counters רבי יהודה with a story that supports the first ruling.
steps.raayaObject: That sleeping under a bed does not fulfill the obligation.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבן גמליאל's remark explaining why his exempt slave slept under the bed.

steps.title: The lesson learned in passing: sleeping under the bed does not count
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון draws the conclusion. From רבן גמליאל's casual remark, we learn that sleeping under a bed does not fulfill the obligation.
steps.simpleTranslation: And by the way, we learned that one who sleeps under the bed has not fulfilled his obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון finishes his proof. He states clearly what we learn 'along the way' from רבן גמליאל's words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If an exempt person sleeps under the bed *because* he is exempt, then an obligated person who sleeps there has not done the מצוה. This brings us back to the first ruling of the משנה.
steps.whatToRemember: The תנא קמא and רבי שמעון say a bed blocks the סכך, so sleeping under it does not count. רבי יהודה allows it, based on the זקנים' silence.

phrases.english: And by the way:
phrases.notes: The lesson comes indirectly, not from a formal ruling.

phrases.english: we learned that one who sleeps under the bed
has not fulfilled his obligation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the halachic inference from the story in the previous step.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: According to רבי שמעון, sleeping under a bed in the סוכה does not fulfill the מצוה.

steps.title: But the space under the bed is less than ten handbreadths
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: a space under ten טפחים does not count as a tent, so how can a bed block the סכך?
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: But there are not ten handbreadths!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and immediately challenges the משנה's first ruling. A normal bed is not ten טפחים high, so why should it count as a barrier?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In הלכה, a covering lower than ten טפחים is not considered a real tent (אהל). If the bed is not a halachic tent, it should not separate the sleeper from the סכך.

keyTerms.meaning: גמרא: the start of the Talmud's discussion
Ten handbreadths, the minimum height for a halachic tent

phrases.english: Gemara:
But there are not ten [handbreadths]!
phrases.notes: A normal bed is too low to be a tent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the basic ruling of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that sleeping under a bed does not fulfill the obligation.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A structure under ten טפחים is not an אהל, so a typical bed should not separate the person from the סכך.

steps.title: שמואל: the משנה is about a bed ten טפחים high
steps.stepSummary: שמואל explains that the משנה is talking about a tall bed, one that is ten טפחים high.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל explained it: with a bed of ten handbreadths.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers the question. He narrows the case in the משנה to a bed that is tall enough to count as a tent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer changes the case, not the rule. A bed that is ten טפחים high is a real אהל, so it does block the סכך. A lower bed would not be a problem.

keyTerms.meaning: שמואל, an early אמורא of בבל

steps.whyThisMatters: This tells us the משנה's ruling applies only to a bed at least ten טפחים high.

phrases.english: Shmuel explained it
as referring to a bed of ten [handbreadths].
phrases.notes: Tall enough to be a halachic tent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by limiting the case of the משנה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to be about any ordinary bed, even one under ten טפחים.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about a bed ten טפחים high, which counts as an אהל and blocks the סכך.

steps.title: A משנה elsewhere: natural hollows count as a tent
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה about טומאת מת. Holes formed naturally, and gaps in stacks of stones or beams, all count as an אהל over טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה elsewhere: a hole carved out by water, by creeping creatures, or eaten away by salt, and also a stack of stones, and also a pile of beams, all count as a covering (אהל) over טומאה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings in a new source from another place (the laws of טומאת מת) to explore what counts as an אהל. This is setting up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the laws of טומאת מת, anything under the same covering as a dead body becomes טמא. This משנה's first opinion says that even a covering no person made, like a hollow in a rock formed by water, still counts as an אהל. Everything on this list formed without anyone intending to build a covering.

keyTerms.meaning: "We learned there." It introduces a משנה from a different place in ש״ס.
Small creeping creatures, such as rodents or insects.
A row or stack of stones with gaps between them.
Acts as a covering over טומאה, so the טומאה spreads to everything underneath.

steps.confusionAlert: Here אהל does not mean a camping tent. It is a halachic category: any covering that spreads טומאת מת to whatever is beneath it.

phrases.english: We learned there (in a mishna):
Both a hole that water bored out,
or creeping creatures, or that salt ate away,
and likewise a course of stones,
and likewise a pile of beams —
forms a covering over the impurity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After discussing whether a bed counts as an אהל that blocks the סכך, the גמרא brings a related משנה about what counts as an אהל in general.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תנא קמא holds that naturally formed hollows and gaps in stacked materials count as an אהל for spreading טומאה.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: only a man-made covering counts as a tent
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה disagrees with the תנא קמא. A covering that a person did not make is not an אהל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: any covering not made by human hands is not an אהל.
steps.whatsHappening: Within the same משנה, רבי יהודה argues against the first opinion. He says natural hollows do not count as an אהל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, the deciding factor is who made the covering. If a person made it, it is an אהל; if nature made it, it is not. So in all the cases of the previous step, the טומאה would not spread.

keyTerms.meaning: A covering that halachically spreads טומאה, or creates a separate roof.

steps.whyThisMatters: רבי יהודה's view that a covering must be man-made will need a source. The גמרא's search for that source drives the next part of the סוגיא.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל אֹהֶל שֶׁאֵינוֹ עָשׂוּי בִּידֵי אָדָם —
phrases.english: Any tent that is not made by human hands —
is not a tent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is the dissenting opinion in the same משנה quoted in step 23.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A covering that a person did not make does not have the status of an אהל.

steps.title: What is רבי יהודה's source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יהודה holds that a natural covering is not an אהל.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of רבי יהודה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where רבי יהודה learns his rule. This question sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה's rule adds a condition, human making, that the תנא קמא does not require. The גמרא wants to know what source or logic forces this extra requirement. This is a request for information, not an attack.

keyTerms.meaning: "What is the reason?" It asks for the source or logic behind an opinion.

phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Yehuda?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It asks for the basis of the opinion רבי יהודה stated in step 24.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source or reasoning behind רבי יהודה's rule that only a man-made covering counts as an אהל.
